report.title: 2026 Year-to-Date S&P 500 Sector Performance Summary
report.overview: Six months into 2026, the market is decisively risk-on. Four sectors are posting double-digit gains while the three laggards are all within 4% of breakeven, suggesting the selloffs are sector-specific rather than a broad market retreat. The standout theme is AI-driven capital allocation, which is lifting Technology and creating downstream demand in Industrials and Materials. The rotation story now is where that momentum moves next.

sectors.summary: The clear frontrunner of 2026. A +29.21% YTD gain is being fuelled by AI infrastructure buildout and surging semiconductor demand, with large-cap tech earnings continuing to beat expectations. The MACD is decelerating slightly but the trend remains intact. This is the benchmark every other sector is being measured against.

Second on a YTD basis but the momentum story here has broken down. A -10.8% drop in just the last month and an RSI of 32 approaching oversold territory tells you the early-year oil rally has reversed hard. The YTD number flatters what is now a sector under significant selling pressure. Watch for a stabilisation at current levels before drawing any conclusions about a recovery.

The most technically healthy sector in the market right now. A confirmed golden cross formation, MACD expanding above its signal line, and price sitting above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages make this the most structurally sound trend of 2026. Reshoring tailwinds and a growing defense and aerospace order backlog are the business drivers. This is not a momentum trade — it has fundamental support.

Up +15.21% YTD with improving momentum, yet still sitting 17.5% below its 200-day moving average. That gap tells you this is a recovery in early stages, not a completed one. Infrastructure spending and EV battery supply chain demand are pulling metals and raw materials higher. There is potentially significant runway left if the macro backdrop holds.

A modest +8.33% YTD that reflects defensive inflows earlier in the year during Q1 volatility. The recent -2.8% one-month pullback signals that capital is now rotating out of defensives as risk appetite improves. The sector is not breaking down — it is simply being deprioritised as investors move toward higher-beta opportunities.

A +4.87% YTD headline number hides a deeply troubled technical picture — price sits 25.3% below its 200-day moving average, indicating long-term structural underperformance. The AI data center power demand narrative has provided a partial lift, but interest rate sensitivity continues to cap upside. The PJM framework decision in March 2027 is the key catalyst to monitor for a genuine re-rating.

The most interesting setup in the market right now. Despite a -2.24% YTD return that puts it in the laggard category, Healthcare carries the strongest bullish sentiment score of any sector at 0.432 and has institutional accumulation actively detected. The MACD is improving, price has reclaimed both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and options flow is pointing toward a sector rotation bet. UnitedHealth and Eli Lilly are leading the rebound. The YTD number is backward-looking — the forward signal here is bullish.

A -0.81% YTD return disguises a violent reversal — the sector dropped hard in early 2026 before surging +10.7% over the last three months on deregulation expectations and yield curve normalisation. The problem now is technical exhaustion: an RSI of 80.3 makes this the most overbought sector in the entire market, and price has broken above its upper Bollinger Band. The structural recovery is real, but a short-term pullback from current levels would be consistent with the data.

sectors.status: Worst Performer, No Clear Recovery Signal
sectors.summary: The weakest sector YTD at -3.09% and the technical picture is the most damaged of any sector — price is sitting 26.8% below its 200-day moving average, a gap that reflects structural rather than cyclical weakness. Tesla's 18.97% weight in XLY creates a concentration risk that amplifies volatility in both directions. Sticky inflation, tariff concerns, and soft consumer confidence are the macro headwinds. A +7.4% three-month bounce shows some stabilisation, but there is no confirmed recovery setup here yet.

key_rotation_signal.summary: The dominant capital flow story of mid-2026 is a rotation out of Energy — which carried the YTD leadership early but has collapsed in momentum — and out of Defensive sectors like Staples and Utilities, and into Healthcare, which is showing the strongest institutional accumulation signal in the market, and Financials, which is recovering on deregulation tailwinds. Technology leadership remains fully intact and is not part of the rotation — it is the anchor. The sectors losing capital are the ones that served as safety trades during Q1 volatility. That defensive premium is being unwound as confidence in the broader market improves.
